_doc: Churn-risk signal (Fable report 2026-11-03, data/support-churn-winback-fable-c1/report.md sections 0 and 4; firstmate spec churn-risk-signal-prevent-p1). ONE policy for the prevent signal: the thresholds that decide who is 'waiting on us', the store paths, the kill file, the lane a cancelled user's issue routes to, the immediate-page survey answers, and the list of queues that must sort risk-first within paid. Read by scripts/churn/support_state.py (the nightly sweeps), scripts/churn/risk.py (writer), scripts/churn/weekly_line.py, scripts/churn/risk_reader.py (every consumer) and scripts/churn/cancel_with_open_issue.sh (the alert). Thresholds are DATA on purpose: a threshold moves by PR, never by env, and the reader re-reads the file on every run so a change needs no deploy. Kill file /etc/hydra/churn-risk.disabled stops the consumers' sort override and the alert; the store keeps building (the weekly line and the 60-day baseline stay measurable while a sort is off).

churn_risk._doc: Consumers' sort override. disabled or stale (older than thresholds.risk_max_age_hours) risk.json is NOT a licence to reorder: an absent override leaves each queue's own order in place, which is always safe.

risk._doc: Which stage kinds make a paying user a risk in risk.json (the spec's three classes; proof-with-nothing-sent counts under the pending class because we owe them either way). told_to_wait is NOT here: a user we told to wait is not being dropped, and it stays in the store for the weekly line and the 60-day baseline.

mrr._doc: List price per plan, USD per month (annual / 12) - report section 0's table. Cash MRR runs ~10% lower on 50% regional/offer coupons; the signal ranks on LIST price so a coupon never hides a Business plan behind a discounted Pro.

alert._doc: The hourly cancel-with-open-issue page (spec item 4). Dedup is per user for dedup_days so a cancel-request page and the cancel itself do not double-page, and so a re-subscribe-then-cancel does not re-page the same open issue. on_demand_max bounds the per-run cost of classifying a canceller the nightly sweep has not seen.

lanes._doc: cause class -> the lane that owns the fix (report section 3.1 item 2). The alert names this lane in its page and tags the intake row with it; it never contacts the user.

consumers.how: FOLLOW-UP PR, not this one (scope ruling 2026-11-04 17:16Z: even a 'gated on a missing file' edit is a change to the credit-send path and needs its own review; d2 + Fable review it). The change is one helper and four call sites: churn_order() reorders each finished audience before its check walks it (owing-uvn, receipts-received, need-asks, reply-due, and the filtered claim list). The lists' signing headers hash a SORTED list of per-user facts, so a reorder cannot invalidate a build; the tick never edits a list's membership.

FOLLOW-UP PR, not this one (same scope ruling). order_rows() prepends risk.sort_key() to the paid/oldest key so it applies to every mode that reads the held queue (judge and, when the writer is on, apply). The import must stay lazy and defensive: a missing churn module or an unreadable policy leaves the old order and stops nothing. The same key orders the day's asks through the same function.

consumers.file: claim lane's list builder (claim-lane-resume-c2, not in this repo)
consumers.how: one line before signing the built list: python3 /opt/hydra/scripts/churn/risk_reader.py order --file <list.json>. Exit is always 0 (fail-open); the signed_on/facts header survives a reorder by design.

consumers.file: merge intake reader (merge-queue-clear-q1, not in this repo)
consumers.how: python3 /opt/hydra/scripts/churn/risk_reader.py order --file <intake.json> --array <array-key> before taking the day's work, or import churn.risk_reader and sort with risk.sort_key(row['user_id']).
same one line on the drain list: risk-first inside paid, renews-soonest first. Never a filter: the reader can only move someone earlier.
